conflicts.point: Whether bio/cyber uplift capability collapses fully into the pre-deployment evaluation gate, or whether a residual portion surfaces only under post-release tool composition and belongs in the standing regime.

positions.stance: Uplift surfaces in pre-deployment capability evaluations run under existing preparedness frameworks, so a capability visible at the bench fires the eval gate both sides accept and needs no separate standing regime; the standing gate should cover only members that are genuinely eval-invisible until first success, of which weight exfiltration is the clearest.

Uplift is only partially eval-visible, because a bounded elicitation protocol samples a fixed prompt-scaffold-tool surface while outside actors compose new tools and jailbreak the harness after release, so the gap between bench-measured ceiling and real-world ceiling stays in the standing tail.

conflicts.point: Whether a behavioral, ex-post trigger has a structurally smaller capture surface than a negotiated ex-ante number, and whether the residual capture point (the elicitation protocol) can be adequately defended.

positions.stance: Whoever writes the definition of the triggering capability controls the gate's reach, and a definition is a capturable object in a way an evaluator's integrity is not; the EU AI Act's 10^25 FLOPS line was set through lobbying, showing the definition itself is the vulnerable joint.

A behavioral trigger applied to observed conduct cannot be lobbied out of, because the model already exhibits the capability; the residual capture surface shrinks to the elicitation protocol, which is defended by a non-industry standard-setter, a standing adversarial challenge process, and periodic public review.

verdicts.conflict: Whether bio/cyber uplift collapses fully into the pre-deployment evaluation gate, or whether a residual portion surfaces only under post-release tool composition and belongs in a standing regime.
verdicts.rationale: C21 cites a specific documented source (the 2026 International AI Safety Report on models performing complex biological tasks including viral evolution prediction) and offers a mechanism for why bench measurement undercounts: a bounded elicitation protocol samples a fixed prompt-scaffold-tool surface while external actors compose new tools after release. C17 asserts uplift 'shows up in pre-deployment evaluations' but supplies no evidence that the bench ceiling equals the deployed ceiling, which is the contested claim. On logical validity C17 is also weaker because it concedes the eval gate exists yet assumes the elicitation surface is complete without defending that assumption.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical measurement showing that adversarial post-release elicitation does not meaningfully exceed the bench-measured capability ceiling — i.e., that a well-designed elicitation protocol captures the real-world maximum — would flip the verdict toward C17.

verdicts.conflict: Whether a behavioral ex-post trigger has a structurally smaller capture surface than a negotiated ex-ante number, and whether the residual capture point (the elicitation protocol) can be adequately defended.
verdicts.rationale: C19 supplies a concrete instance of capture at the definitional joint — the EU AI Act's 10^25 FLOPS line set through lobbying — demonstrating that a triggering definition is a capturable object in practice. C22 offers a plausible structural argument that an ex-post behavioral trigger measures conduct that did not exist when the definition was written, but its proposed defenses (non-industry standard-setter, adversarial challenge process, periodic review) are asserted design features with no track record cited. C22 also does not fully rebut C19's core point, because the elicitation protocol and the capability definition it operationalizes remain written in advance and thus remain a capturable surface; the argument shifts the capture point rather than eliminating it.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that behavioral or conduct-based regulatory triggers in an analogous domain resisted capture better than numeric thresholds, or a demonstration that an independently governed elicitation protocol held up against sustained industry pressure, would strengthen C22 above C19.
